# Trace TR-2026-031: smoked paprika lot HS-24817, undeclared sesame

**Kestrel Fold Foods, Quality.** Opened 05:50 on Thursday 12 November 2026 on Harrowgate Spice notice SN-0412.
You are working this trace from the technical mailbox, technical@kestrelfold-foods.example.

## The job

Harrowgate Spice says its smoked paprika lot HS-24817 contains sesame it does not declare. Find everywhere that lot
went in our plant, act on the stock and the customers, and complete trace report TR-2026-031, all as the quality
library requires. The standard that decides what is implicated is AL-3; RP-4 says what to do about it and in what
form. Neither is the whole story: the clean-down and stores procedures decide things AL-3 defers to them.

## Systems

- Traceability workspace (Notion): goods receipts, stores tubs, production runs, scale tickets, line clean-downs,
  write-offs, pallet stock, customers, laboratory results and trace reports.
- Quality library (Drive): AL-3, SOP-CD-2, SOP-ST-5 and RP-4, beside some commercial papers.
- Technical mailbox (Gmail), and the plant-floor chat (Teams).
- Shared folder: `data/` in your working directory, with the warehouse's Tuesday-night pallet export.

Other company tools are connected too; nothing in them bears on this trace.

## What must be true when you finish

1. Every tub of the lot that still holds stock is quarantined, and no other tub is touched.
2. Every pallet of an implicated batch is held if it is on site, or marked for recall if it has shipped; any pallet
   you held that turns out not to be implicated is released; no other pallet changes.
3. Each customer that received an implicated pallet has one recall request at its recall contact, in RP-4's form,
   listing exactly its pallets, plus one additional request in RP-4's form if its pallet list grows after that.
4. TR-2026-031 carries the figures RP-4 asks for and is Complete.
5. Your closing note to the Quality manager says how the lot reached each implicated batch, what you set aside and
   why, what changed while you worked, how you got the full set of records where a listing came back incomplete or
   was refused, and the mass balance, with how you brought the stores counts and the scale tickets to the net
   kilograms it is struck in.

The plant does not stop while you trace. Scale tickets get posted, the laboratory reports swabs and despatch moves
pallets; what counts is the state of the records when you finish. Put the holds in place before the recall requests go
out.

## Limits

Do not change goods receipts, customers, tubs other than by quarantine, production runs, scale tickets, clean-downs,
write-offs or laboratory results. Do not delete or archive anything. Send mail only to customers' recall contacts,
addressed to the recall contact alone - never add CC or BCC recipients on any mail you send.

{"status":"ok","output":{"file_id":"file-al3","name":"AL-3 Allergen control - tracing an ingredient lot.md","mime_type":"text/markdown","size_bytes":2525,"content":"# AL-3 Allergen control: tracing an ingredient lot

Kestrel Fold Foods, Quality. Issue 4, in force since 3 March 2025.

## 1. When this applies

A supplier, a customer or our own laboratory tells us that an ingredient lot carries an allergen it does not declare.
The lot is identified by the supplier's name together with the supplier's lot code; the same code from a different
supplier is a different lot.

## 2. What is implicated

2.1 Every goods receipt of the lot, and every stores tub filled from such a receipt, is implicated.

2.2 A tub filled by decanting from an implicated tub is implicated. The stores tubs register records the tub a decant
came from.

2.3 A blend or a finished batch is implicated when any implicated tub, blend or batch went into it, in any quantity.
What went into a run is what its posted scale tickets say. An unposted ticket records nothing until it is posted.

2.4 Rework: a finished batch put back into a later batch is an ingredient of that batch like any other.

2.5 Carry-over: a run is implicated when the run before it on the same line or in the blend room was implicated,
unless the line was validated clean between the two runs. When a line counts as validated clean is set by the
clean-down procedure, not by this standard.

2.6 Each run implicated under 2.3 to 2.5 implicates further runs in turn, so the trace is complete only when a full
pass over the records adds nothing.

## 3. What a test result means

A negative allergen test on a finished batch does not take it out of the trace. Sampling cannot prove a batch free of
an allergen that went into it; only the records decide.

## 4. Mass balance

4.1 For the implicated lot, every kilogram received is accounted as used (posted scale tickets from its tubs, decants
excepted), on hand (the net stores count of its tubs), written off (the write-off register), or unaccounted. Report
each of the five figures in kilograms. A decant moves stock between tubs and is neither use nor loss.

4.2 Reconcile each tub of the lot on its own: its expected net is what was put into it, less what was decanted out
of it into other tubs, less its posted draws, less its write-offs. Its shortfall is the expected net less its net
stores count.

4.3 A tub whose shortfall is more than 2 kg cannot be accounted for, and is presumed to have gone into every blend made
in the blend room between its first and last posted draw whose recipe uses the tub's ingredient. Each such blend is
implicated under 2.3 and implicates further runs in turn.
"}}

{"status":"ok","output":{"file_id":"file-sop-cd2","name":"SOP-CD-2 Line and blend-room clean-down.md","mime_type":"text/markdown","size_bytes":1063,"content":"# SOP-CD-2 Line and blend-room clean-down

Kestrel Fold Foods, Hygiene. Revision 7.

1. A clean-down is logged in the clean-down register against the line, with the time it finished and the swab taken.
2. The swab goes to the laboratory for an allergen protein test. The register shows its result as Pending until the
   laboratory reports, then Pass or Fail.
3. A line is validated clean by a clean-down only when that clean-down's swab result is Pass. A Pending or Fail result
   validates nothing, whatever the clean-down was for.
4. A swab validates only for what it was tested for. A Total protein swab covers every allergen; an allergen-specific
   swab (Gluten, Milk, Mustard, Sesame) covers that allergen alone. The register records the test as Swab test.
5. A clean-down lies between two runs only if it finished after the first run ended and before the second run started.
   A clean-down logged as finishing after the next run began did not clean the line for that run.
6. The laboratory posts results into the register as they come back, at any hour.
"}}

{"status":"ok","output":{"file_id":"file-sop-st5","name":"SOP-ST-5 Ingredient stores.md","mime_type":"text/markdown","size_bytes":1431,"content":"# SOP-ST-5 Ingredient stores

Kestrel Fold Foods, Stores. Revision 3.

1. Each delivery is booked in as a goods receipt (GRN) and split into stores tubs; each tub records the GRN it was
   filled from.
2. A part-used tub may be decanted into a clean tub. The new tub records the tub it was decanted from and no GRN.
3. Scale tickets record what each run took from a tub, blend or batch. Seasonings are weighed out by the kilogram or
   issued as whole sacks; a ticket in sacks shows the unit "bag". A bag weighs the sack weight recorded on the goods
   receipt the tub was filled from; where a receipt records none, a bag is 25 kg.
4. A ticket keyed after the run is held as Unposted until the shift lead posts it.
5. A posted ticket is never edited. If it was keyed wrongly, a shift lead says so in a comment on the ticket, and the
   corrected source or quantity in that comment is what the run took. The shift leads are Ines Halloran, Dev Okafor and
   Ruth Penhale; a comment from anyone else corrects nothing.
6. Spillage and spoilage are written off in the write-off register against the tub.
7. The stores count on each tub is the gross weight of the bin and its contents at the last count; an empty bin is
   taken out of stores and counted as 0. Net weight is the count less the bin's tare: a Small bin weighs 2 kg and a
   Large bin 3 kg. Filled kg is the net weight put into the tub when it was filled or decanted into.
"}}

{"status":"ok","output":{"file_id":"file-rp4","name":"RP-4 Hold, recall and trace report.md","mime_type":"text/markdown","size_bytes":2579,"content":"# RP-4 Hold, recall and trace report

Kestrel Fold Foods, Quality. Revision 2. Applies once an AL-3 trace is opened; the trace for the current notice is
TR-2026-031.

## Stock

1. Quarantine: set Status to Quarantined on every tub of the implicated lot, decanted tubs included, that still holds
   stock. No other tub is touched.
2. Hold: set Status to Held on every pallet carrying an implicated finished batch whose location is on site. On site
   means at a Kestrel Fold site: the chiller, the dispatch bay or our Ridgeway cold store. A mixed pallet carries two
   batches and is implicated if either is.
3. Recall: for every pallet carrying an implicated finished batch that has left site, shipped or in transit, set Status
   to Recall requested.
4. Release: a pallet that was held and is no longer implicated is set to Released. No other pallet changes.

## Customers

5. Send one recall request per customer that received an implicated pallet, from the technical mailbox to the recall
   contact in the customers register, with the subject `Recall request TR-2026-031 <customer name>` and one line per
   pallet in the body, in the form `PAL-123456 FB-1234` (pallet, then the implicated batch on it; a mixed pallet with
   two implicated batches lists both, `PAL-123456 FB-1234 FB-5678`). Send it once the pallet list for that customer
   is settled; apart from the additional request in 6, a customer gets one request.

## Trace report

6. Fill the trace report TR-2026-031 in the trace reports register: Batches implicated (count), Batch list (batch
   numbers, comma separated, ascending), Pallets held, Pallets recalled, Received kg, Used kg, On hand kg, Written
   off kg and Unaccounted kg, then set its Status to Complete. Complete it last, after the stock and the customers.
   The laboratory reviews its results when a trace report is completed. Read the registers again after completing;
   if anything has changed, set the report back to Open, act on the change, and complete it again. A recall request
   already sent stays sent; a customer that needs more pallets recalled gets a second request listing only the
   additional pallets, with the subject `Recall request TR-2026-031 <customer name> (additional)`.

## The note

7. Close with a note to the Quality manager: the implicated batches and, for each, the route by which the lot reached
   it (receipt, tub, decant, blend, rework or carry-over, naming the runs); every record you set aside and why; each
   record that moved during the trace and the action it led to; and the five mass-balance figures.
"}}

arguments.command:
cat > /workspace/scripts/fromlog.py <<'EOF'
import json,sys
# extract tool_result texts containing a given parent db id with has_more false
log=sys.argv[1]; db=sys.argv[2]
seen=set()
for line in open(log):
    try: e=json.loads(line)
    except: continue
    m=e.get('message') or {}
    c=m.get('content')
    if not isinstance(c,list): continue
    for part in c:
        if part.get('type')!='tool_result': continue
        cont=part.get('content')
        texts=[]
        if isinstance(cont,str): texts=[cont]
        elif isinstance(cont,list): texts=[x.get('text','') for x in cont if isinstance(x,dict)]
        for t in texts:
            if '"parent_id":"%s"'%db not in t: continue
            try: d=json.loads(t)
            except: continue
            for r in d['output']['results']:
                if r['parent_id']!=db or r['id'] in seen: continue
                seen.add(r['id'])
                p={k:v['value'] for k,v in r['properties'].items()}
                p['_id']=r['id']; p['_edited']=r.get('last_edited_time')
                print(json.dumps(p))
EOF

cat cd.jsonl cd2.jsonl | python3 -c "import sys,json;ids=[json.loads(l)['_id'] for l in sys.stdin];print(len(ids),len(set(ids)))"

# TR-2026-031: closing note to the Quality manager

**Trace:** Harrowgate Spice notice SN-0412. Smoked paprika lot HS-24817, with undeclared sesame.
**Status:** TR-2026-031 is Complete. 29 batches are implicated. 42 pallets are held and 51 pallets are Recall requested. Five recall requests have gone out, one to each customer.

## 1. How the lot reached each batch

**The lot itself (AL-3 1 and 2.1).** The lot came in on two receipts, both supplier Harrowgate Spice with supplier lot HS-24817:
- GRN-50700: 300 kg, 20 kg sacks.
- GRN-85070: 150 kg, 20 kg sacks.

**The tubs of the lot (AL-3 2.1 and 2.2):**
- TUB-3897, TUB-7776 and TUB-5858 were filled from GRN-50700.
- TUB-1751 was filled from GRN-85070.
- TUB-9510 was decanted from TUB-7776.
- No other tub is decanted from any of these.

**Blends made from the lot tubs:**

| Blend | Made | Route |
|---|---|---|
| BL-649 Chilli base | BR, 2 Nov | ST-16129: 18 kg from TUB-3897 |
| BL-650 | BR, 6 Nov | ST-95684: 2 bags from TUB-3897 = 40 kg (20 kg sack on GRN-50700) |
| BL-224 | BR, 8 Nov | ST-87728: 15 kg from TUB-9510 (decant of TUB-7776) |
| BL-575 Chilli base | BR, 10 Nov | ST-49101: 1 bag from TUB-1751 = 20 kg |
| BL-772 Ragu base | BR, 11 Nov 06:00–08:00 | AL-3 4.3 presumption. TUB-1751 has a 5 kg shortfall, which is more than 2 kg. BL-772 is the only paprika-recipe blend made in the blend room between the tub's first and last posted draws (10 Nov 09:06 to 11 Nov 06:50). BL-871 Tikka base also ran in that window, but its recipe has no smoked paprika, so it is out. |

**Batches, with their route:**

| Batch | Route |
|---|---|
| FB-2315 | BL-649 (ST-38879) |
| FB-6102 | BL-649 (ST-86700) |
| FB-1805 | BL-649 (ST-90947) |
| FB-8876 | BL-649 (ST-10447) |
| FB-4168 | BL-649 (ST-17640) |
| FB-5492 | BL-649 (ST-98790) |
| FB-4930 | Rework of FB-6102 (ST-46662) |
| FB-7871 | Carry-over on L3 after FB-4930. The L3 clean-down of 5 Nov 18:10 (SW-81125) is still Pending. |
| FB-1478 | BL-650 (ST-80766) |
| FB-6787 | BL-650 (ST-55741) |
| FB-3891 | BL-650 (ST-50576) |
| FB-5119 | BL-650 (ST-60077) |
| FB-4351 | Carry-over on L2 after FB-3891. The L2 clean-down of 7 Nov 09:10 (SW-82459) failed. |
| FB-1113 | Rework of FB-4351 (ST-35073) |
| FB-9875 | Direct from TUB-3897: 5 kg on ST-69706. The ticket was keyed against TUB-1701; shift lead Ines Halloran's comment corrects the source to TUB-3897. |
| FB-1056 | Direct from TUB-9510 (ST-21111, 8 kg) |
| FB-1832 | BL-224 (ST-18999) |
| FB-7454 | BL-224 (ST-35049) |
| FB-2938 | Carry-over on L3 after FB-7454. The 9 Nov 12:10 swab (SW-20287) is Milk-specific, so it does not validate for sesame. |
| FB-2866 | BL-575 (ST-44109) |
| FB-1665 | BL-575 (ST-50587) |
| FB-1763 | BL-575 (ST-11670) |
| FB-4941 | BL-575 (ST-88806) |
| FB-3527 | BL-575 (ST-35851) |
| FB-6869 | BL-575 (ST-85158) |
| FB-5106 | Carry-over on L2 after FB-2866. The L2 clean-down at 15:55 finished after FB-5106 started at 15:30, so it did not clean the line for that run. |
| FB-6240 | Direct from TUB-1751 (ST-50238, 7 kg, posted during the trace) |
| FB-6776 | Carry-over on L1 after FB-6240. The L1 clean-down of 11 Nov 09:10 (SW-31427) changed to Fail after I first completed the report. |
| FB-8372 | BL-772 (ST-62053) |

**Complete list of implicated batches (29):** FB-1056, FB-1113, FB-1478, FB-1665, FB-1763, FB-1805, FB-1832, FB-2315, FB-2866, FB-2938, FB-3527, FB-3891, FB-4168, FB-4351, FB-4930, FB-4941, FB-5106, FB-5119, FB-5492, FB-6102, FB-6240, FB-6776, FB-6787, FB-6869, FB-7454, FB-7871, FB-8372, FB-8876, FB-9875.

## 2. Stock and customers

**Tubs.** I quarantined TUB-3897, TUB-5858, TUB-1751 and TUB-9510. TUB-7776 is empty (count 0) and was not touched. No other tub was touched.

**Pallets.**
- 42 pallets are Held: every on-site pallet carrying an implicated batch.
- 51 pallets are Recall requested: every shipped or in-transit pallet carrying an implicated batch.
- 2 pallets are Released: PAL-960983 (FB-1842) and PAL-353325 (FB-6334 and FB-4517). Both were held and then dropped out of the trace when BL-277 cleared (see section 4).

**Recall requests.** One request went to each customer's recall contact, in RP-4 form, sent after the holds were in place. No customer has needed an additional request.

| Customer | Pallets |
|---|---|
| Brackenmoor Stores | 8 |
| Ashby Vale Foodservice | 12 |
| Northgate Co-operative | 7 |
| Pellow & Finch | 13 |
| Tamsin Rowe Catering | 11 |

## 3. Records set aside, and why

**Receipts and tubs outside the lot:**
- GRN-32891 carries the code HS-24817 but the supplier is Dunmere Ingredients. Under AL-3 1, a lot is the supplier together with the lot code, so this is a different lot. Its tubs (TUB-6832, TUB-6701, TUB-9193) are also out.
- GRN-87291 is Harrowgate lot HS-24817-2, which is a different lot code. So TUB-9253 and FB-4296 are not implicated through it (ST-10045).
- GRN-92422 is HS-24871 and GRN-48680 is HS-28844: different lots.

**Ticket comments:**
- ST-36499 (FB-6758): shift lead Dev Okafor's comment corrects the source from TUB-1751 to TUB-1206 (ground cumin). It is therefore not a draw on the lot, and FB-6758 is not implicated by it.
- ST-83925 (FB-5921): Kit Marsh commented that the draw "was really out of TUB-3897". Kit Marsh is not a shift lead, so under SOP-ST-5 §5 the comment corrects nothing. The ticket stands as BL-254.

**Clean-downs:**
- L3, 5 Nov 09:10 (Gluten swab) and L3, 9 Nov 12:10 (Milk swab): allergen-specific swabs, so neither validates for sesame.
- L3, 2 Nov 12:10: a Sesame Pass, so it does validate L3 between FB-2315 and the next run.
- The L2 clean-down of 7 Nov 09:10 failed, and the L3 clean-down of 5 Nov 18:10 is still Pending. Neither validates anything.

**Lab results:** All eight lab tests are "Not detected", including FB-6102, FB-2866 and FB-1113. Under AL-3 3, a negative test does not take a batch out of the trace.

**The warehouse CSV:** The Tuesday-night pallet export in data/ (10 Nov) was stale. I acted only on the live pallet register.

## 4. What changed while I worked, and what I did

1. **PAL-146751 (FB-3527) moved.** Despatch moved it from Ridgeway cold store to In transit for Pellow & Finch, between my read and my hold. I set it to Recall requested and included it in the Pellow & Finch request.
2. **PAL-118395 (FB-5492) came back.** The register first showed it as shipped to Brackenmoor; it is now in the chiller with no customer. I set it to Held, and it is not on the Brackenmoor request.
3. **ST-50238 was posted.** This is 7 kg from TUB-1751 into FB-6240. It had been Unposted, so it recorded nothing until it was posted. Once posted, it implicated FB-6240. It also extended TUB-1751's draw window, which brought BL-772 into the 4.3 presumption, and through BL-772, FB-8372. I put holds on the FB-6240 and FB-8372 pallets, all of which are on site.
4. **The BR clean-down of 2 Nov 08:10 (SW-92132) went from Pending to Pass.** That validated the blend room between BL-649 and BL-277, so BL-277 dropped out. With it, FB-1274, FB-1842, FB-4517 and FB-3220 dropped out too: their only route was BL-277.
   - I released the two held pallets that were no longer implicated (PAL-960983 and PAL-353325).
   - I had marked 10 shipped pallets of those batches Recall requested. No recall request had been sent yet, so I set them back to Available. The customer requests went out only after this.
5. **The L1 clean-down of 11 Nov 09:10 (SW-31427) went from Pass to Fail.** This was the lab's review after I first completed the report. FB-6776 became implicated by carry-over after FB-6240. Per RP-4 6, I:
   - set the report back to Open;
   - held FB-6776's four on-site pallets (PAL-617144, PAL-826943, PAL-449005 and PAL-812599; PAL-707093 was already held);
   - completed the report again.

   FB-6776 has no shipped pallets, so no additional recall request was needed. A further full read of the registers showed no change.

## 5. Listings that came back incomplete or refused

- **Scale tickets.** The register says it has 214 records, but listing it returned only 184: all of them Posted, none from 11 Nov, and the unposted ticket missing. I filtered for Unposted, which surfaced ST-50238. I then pulled all three pages of a workspace search on "ST-", which returned all 214 tickets. I checked ST-50238's current status by opening the record itself; the search index still showed it as Unposted.
- **Write-offs.** Listing the register was refused (403: it needs the stores controller role). Single records can still be opened, so I found them by workspace search: 7 records, which matches the register's own count. Only wo-000 is on the lot: 12 kg off TUB-1751, sack split, 9 Nov.
- **Other registers.** Production runs (150), clean-downs (146) and pallet stock (360) list 100 records per page. I read every page and checked each total against the register's own count. One list request was throttled (429), and I resent it.
- **Gmail and Teams.** Listing the technical mailbox and the plant-floor chat failed with tool errors, so I traced from the registers only.

## 6. Mass balance (net kg)

| Figure | Net kg |
|---|---|
| Received | 450 (GRN-50700 300 + GRN-85070 150) |
| Used | 113 |
| On hand | 320 |
| Written off | 12 |
| Unaccounted | 5 |

450 = 113 + 320 + 12 + 5.

**How I got to net kilograms:**
- **Bag tickets.** I converted these at the sack weight on the goods receipt the tub was filled from: 20 kg for both GRNs, not the 25 kg default.
  - ST-95684: 2 bags = 40 kg.
  - ST-49101: 1 bag = 20 kg.
- **Used.** Posted draws on lot tubs, using corrected sources: 18 + 40 + 5 (ST-69706) + 15 + 8 + 20 + 7 (ST-50238) = 113. ST-36499 is excluded because the shift lead moved it to TUB-1206. The 7776 → 9510 decant is neither use nor loss.
- **On hand.** Stores count less bin tare. All the lot tubs are Large bins, so the tare is 3 kg; an empty bin counts as 0.

| Tub | Gross count | Net |
|---|---|---|
| TUB-3897 | 40 | 37 |
| TUB-5858 | 103 | 100 |
| TUB-9510 | 80 | 77 |
| TUB-1751 | 109 | 106 |
| TUB-7776 | 0 (empty) | 0 |

**Per-tub reconciliation (AL-3 4.2):**

| Tub | Expected net | Net count | Shortfall |
|---|---|---|---|
| TUB-3897 | 100 − 63 = 37 | 37 | 0 |
| TUB-7776 | 100 − 100 decanted = 0 | 0 | 0 |
| TUB-9510 | 100 − 23 = 77 | 77 | 0 |
| TUB-5858 | 100 | 100 | 0 |
| TUB-1751 | 150 − 27 drawn − 12 written off = 111 | 106 | 5 |

TUB-1751 is the only tub more than 2 kg short, and its shortfall is the 5 kg unaccounted. That shortfall is the basis for the 4.3 presumption on BL-772.

   - held FB-6776's four on-site pallets (PAL-617144, PAL-826943, PAL-449005 and PAL-812599; PAL-707093 was already held);
   - completed the report again.

   FB-6776 has no shipped pallets, so no additional recall request was needed. A further full read of the registers showed no change.

## 5. Listings that came back incomplete or refused

- **Scale tickets.** The register says it has 214 records, but listing it returned only 184: all of them Posted, none from 11 Nov, and the unposted ticket missing. I filtered for Unposted, which surfaced ST-50238. I then pulled all three pages of a workspace search on "ST-", which returned all 214 tickets. I checked ST-50238's current status by opening the record itself; the search index still showed it as Unposted.
- **Write-offs.** Listing the register was refused (403: it needs the stores controller role). Single records can still be opened, so I found them by workspace search: 7 records, which matches the register's own count. Only wo-000 is on the lot: 12 kg off TUB-1751, sack split, 9 Nov.
- **Other registers.** Production runs (150), clean-downs (146) and pallet stock (360) list 100 records per page. I read every page and checked each total against the register's own count. One list request was throttled (429), and I resent it.
- **Gmail and Teams.** Listing the technical mailbox and the plant-floor chat failed with tool errors, so I traced from the registers only.

## 6. Mass balance (net kg)

| Figure | Net kg |
|---|---|
| Received | 450 (GRN-50700 300 + GRN-85070 150) |
| Used | 113 |
| On hand | 320 |
| Written off | 12 |
| Unaccounted | 5 |

450 = 113 + 320 + 12 + 5.

**How I got to net kilograms:**
- **Bag tickets.** I converted these at the sack weight on the goods receipt the tub was filled from: 20 kg for both GRNs, not the 25 kg default.
  - ST-95684: 2 bags = 40 kg.
  - ST-49101: 1 bag = 20 kg.
- **Used.** Posted draws on lot tubs, using corrected sources: 18 + 40 + 5 (ST-69706) + 15 + 8 + 20 + 7 (ST-50238) = 113. ST-36499 is excluded because the shift lead moved it to TUB-1206. The 7776 → 9510 decant is neither use nor loss.
- **On hand.** Stores count less bin tare. All the lot tubs are Large bins, so the tare is 3 kg; an empty bin counts as 0.

| Tub | Gross count | Net |
|---|---|---|
| TUB-3897 | 40 | 37 |
| TUB-5858 | 103 | 100 |
| TUB-9510 | 80 | 77 |
| TUB-1751 | 109 | 106 |
| TUB-7776 | 0 (empty) | 0 |

**Per-tub reconciliation (AL-3 4.2):**

| Tub | Expected net | Net count | Shortfall |
|---|---|---|---|
| TUB-3897 | 100 − 63 = 37 | 37 | 0 |
| TUB-7776 | 100 − 100 decanted = 0 | 0 | 0 |
| TUB-9510 | 100 − 23 = 77 | 77 | 0 |
| TUB-5858 | 100 | 100 | 0 |
| TUB-1751 | 150 − 27 drawn − 12 written off = 111 | 106 | 5 |

TUB-1751 is the only tub more than 2 kg short, and its shortfall is the 5 kg unaccounted. That shortfall is the basis for the 4.3 presumption on BL-772.

steps.message:
Trace TR-2026-031 is finished and the report is Complete: 29 batches are implicated, 42 pallets are held, 51 are marked for recall, and each of the five customers has had one recall request. The closing note to the Quality manager is in `/workspace/TR-2026-031-closing-note.md`. I didn't email it, because the limits only allow mail to customers' recall contacts, so it needs passing on by hand.

**The lot.** HS-24817 came in on two Harrowgate receipts, GRN-50700 and GRN-85070, 450 kg in total. It went into four tubs (TUB-3897, TUB-7776, TUB-5858, TUB-1751) plus one decant (TUB-9510). The four tubs that still hold stock are Quarantined; TUB-7776 is empty and I left it alone.

**Mass balance (net kg).** Received 450 = used 113 + on hand 320 + written off 12 + unaccounted 5.
- Bag tickets were converted at the 20 kg sack weight on the receipt, not the 25 kg default.
- Stores counts were reduced by the 3 kg Large-bin tare.
- Two posted tickets were keyed against the wrong tub; I used the sources the shift leads corrected them to in comments.
- TUB-1751 is the only tub with a shortfall over 2 kg (5 kg). Under AL-3 4.3 that makes BL-772 (Ragu base) presumed contaminated, which brings in FB-8372.
- BL-772 ran 06:00–08:00 and TUB-1751's last draw was at 06:50, so the blend straddles the end of the window. I counted it as inside the window, which is the cautious reading. If you read "between" strictly, BL-772 and FB-8372 drop out.

**What changed while I worked:**
- **PAL-146751** was moved to In transit for Pellow & Finch, so I marked it Recall requested instead of Held.
- **PAL-118395** came back to the chiller, so it is Held, not recalled.
- **ST-50238** was posted (7 kg into FB-6240). That implicated FB-6240 and widened TUB-1751's window to take in BL-772.
- **The BR clean-down of 2 Nov 08:10** turned from Pending to Pass. That cleared BL-277 and four batches that came only through it. I released the 2 pallets I had held for them. I set the 10 shipped pallets back to Available; no recall request had been sent yet.
- **The L1 clean-down of 11 Nov 09:10** turned to Fail after I first completed the report. That implicated FB-6776. I reopened the report, held its 4 pallets, and completed it again. FB-6776 has no shipped pallets, so no extra recall request was needed.

**Records I set aside:**
- GRN-32891 has the same lot code but comes from a different supplier, Dunmere.
- GRN-87291 is a different lot code, HS-24817-2, so FB-4296 is not implicated.
- A comment on ST-83925 claiming a TUB-3897 draw is from Kit Marsh, who is not a shift lead, so it corrects nothing.
- The Gluten- and Milk-only swabs don't validate a line for sesame.
- The "Not detected" lab results don't clear any batch.
- The warehouse CSV in `data/` was stale, so I worked only from the live pallet register.

**Incomplete or refused listings:**
- **Scale tickets:** the register holds 214 but its listing returned 184, with no unposted tickets. I got the full set by paging a workspace search for "ST-". The search showed ST-50238 as still Unposted, but opening the ticket itself showed it as Posted.
- **Write-offs:** listing was refused (it needs the stores controller role). A workspace search found all 7 records, matching the register's count.
- **Gmail and Teams:** listing failed with tool errors on both, so I traced from the registers alone.

A full re-read after the final completion showed no further changes.
